newsitem.title: HUNGARY: U.S. def sec says war crimes suspects "on notice".
newsitem.headline: U.S. def sec says war crimes suspects "on notice".

text.p: Suspected war criminals in Bosnia have been put "on notice" that they will not remain free indefinitely by action against two suspects by NATO-led peacekeeping troops, U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Thursday.

"I think all who are subject to indictment by the War Crimes Tribunal should be on notice that at some point in time that they will be brought to justice," Cohen told reporters in an interview during a visit to Hungary.

The secretary said Thursday's actions that resulted in the arrest of one suspect and shooting death of another by British troops were not a direct result of a warning issued by NATO leaders in Madrid this week to the former warring factions in Bosnia to comply with the Dayton peace accords.
"There has been no political decision made to use the (military arrest) authority that has not been used in the past," Cohen told reporters.
"I believe that there is no connection between the statment (at a NATO sumit) in Madrid and this ... this is not directly related to the Madrid communique," he said.

"I have not issued any such instructions and I do not believe any such instructions have been issued," Cohen replied when asked if he had given orders to U.S. troops in the NATO- led force to more actively go after indicted suspects who they might run across in the normal performance of their military duties.
